chest_pain.title: Chest pain or pressure

steps.text: Stay calm. Stop all activity. Help the crew member rest in a secure, comfortable position and loosen tight clothing.

steps.check: Are they awake and answering you?

steps.text: Clip the sensor on their finger. Keep the hand still for 30 seconds so the readings at the top settle.

steps.check: Is the pain strong, crushing, or spreading to the arm, jaw or back?
Are they short of breath, sweaty, or feeling faint?

steps.text: Give oxygen: put the oxygen mask from the medical kit on them and set the flow the kit card shows. Watch the blood oxygen at the top.
Send the message to the flight surgeon now (panel below). Use the medical kit only as its card or the flight surgeon tells you. Keep them resting for 5 minutes.
Check their breathing: look, listen and feel for 10 seconds.
Stay with them and keep watching the vitals. Do not leave them alone.
steps.check: Have they stopped responding or stopped breathing?

red_flags: Blood oxygen (SpO2) in the danger range
Heart rate in the danger range (very fast or very slow)

unresponsive.title: Crew member not responding

steps.text: Call their name loudly and squeeze their shoulder. Watch their face and hands.
Stop the drift: hold them by the torso (not the arms) and guide them to the nearest wall or the medical restraint area. Call your crew for help now.
Restrain them face up against a firm surface: straps across the chest and hips. Put your own feet in foot loops so you stay in place.
Open the airway: tilt the head back gently, chin up. Look, listen and feel for breathing for 10 seconds.
Feel for a pulse at the side of the neck for up to 10 seconds, or read it on the finger sensor.
Give oxygen: put the oxygen mask from the medical kit on them and set the flow the kit card shows.
Keep them restrained with the airway open and the sensor on their finger. Watch the vitals at the top.
steps.check: Has breathing stopped or turned into gasping?

steps.text: Stay with them, keep them restrained and warm, and send the message to the flight surgeon (panel below).

red_flags: Blood oxygen (SpO2) in the danger range
Heart rate in the danger range (very fast or very slow)
unresponsive._note: Microgravity order: stop the drift and restrain the crew member against a surface first; only then airway, breathing, pulse and CPR. PLACEHOLDER text, based on general first-aid order; Yenna checks against NASA guidance.
